title: Lina's Garden Helpers
markdown:
The warm afternoon sun whispered golden smiles across the garden, painting long mellow shadows. A gentle breeze ambled through the wise old oak, and the little leafy shoots in Lina’s garden swayed like sleepy dancers. Lina knelt near a small stem, finger tracing its slender shape.

“Oh dear,” whispered Auntie June, voice as soft as a well-loved blanket. “Those little stems are swaying so much. Will they be all right?”

“They seem so willing to sway,” murmured Lina. “Why don’t they fall down?”

Moss the hedgehog nudged the dark mellow soil. Little pale threads peeked out. Lina leaned closer. “Look, Moss. These lines go down, down into the ground, always reaching.” She brushed away more soil. Thin pale strands.

They waited a breath. A cloud snagged on the oak and tore itself slowly into blue. The shoots kept dancing and did not fall.

“They look like little helpers,” mused Auntie June.

Lina’s face lit. “The stem helps the leafy shoot reach up for the warm sun. And these roots drink the water from the mellow ground and hold the shoot so it doesn’t blow away. Little hands holding on, so snug.” She patted the soil around the roots, nestling them.

The wind whistled a soft lullaby. The leafy shoots swayed with graceful motion and stayed standing. Stems flexible and strong. Roots like gentle anchors.

Auntie June’s warmth spread. “Stems reach for the mellow light. Roots are their quiet friends, holding them close, drinking good things. They work together.”

Lina looked at the dancing shoots, a quiet peace filling her. Stems for nourishment and light. Roots a steady connection to home. Moss huffed, content, and curled near the base, feeling that hidden strength. The sun dipped, painting the sky in mellow colours. The garden grew quiet, settling into gentle slumber. Lina wondered what other helpers might be working out of sight, down where the soil kept its secrets, and did not need to pull them up to know they were there.
characters: Lina (a patient inventor), Moss (a hedgehog), June (an aunt)
